parts.overview: Ostra runs the Ultracode engineering pipeline on the user's own machine: research, spec, fact-check, plan, build, review, test, and docs. It is one Rust binary, `ostra`, plus a React console that the binary embeds. The binary is split into 15 crates in one Cargo workspace. `ostra-core` holds the shared types and traits. `ostra-engine` holds the event-sourced session state, the pure planner, and the runner. `ostra-exec-native` and `ostra-exec-harness` run agents, either in Ostra's own loop or inside a coding CLI. `ostra-policy` and `ostra-sandbox` contain every tool call and process. `ostra-tools`, `ostra-providers`, `ostra-code`, and `ostra-mcp` supply tools, model clients, code navigation, and MCP servers. `ostra-workspace` and `ostra-store` hold workspaces and SQLite storage. `ostra-server` wires all of these together behind axum, REST, and a WebSocket. Code drives the pipeline and holds every gate. Models do the work inside a stage and answer a small set of named judge questions. The browser talks to the binary over REST for reads and commands, and over one WebSocket at `/ws` for everything live.

subsections.title: Implementation review, format, tests, and docs
subsections.purpose: When every phase of an Implement session has finished, the implementation review gate opens (Rule F1). After the user accepts, the format command runs once per project, and the closing gate asks about tests and docs per project. Tests run EPA in parallel and write-test one phase at a time. Docs run one documentation writer per project, at most MAX_DOCS_WRITERS (4) at once, then system-architecture when two or more projects are documented, then Step::WriteBook.
assumptions: The runner writes ostra-session-context.md from the fold before a revision spawns and before the review gate opens (Rule F2, context::render).
The engine, not an agent, writes the book (Rule B5). ostra_core::book::apply merges parts and writes under <workspace>/.ostra/docs/<book>/.
A book id is the sorted project keys joined with _ (book::book_id), so the next session over the same projects updates the same book (Rule B6).
Nothing is documented while a BLOCKER finding is open in that project.

assumptions: Judge calls always go through Services::judge, which the server implements with ostra_providers::structured on a native provider, so a judge route cannot point at a harness.

sections.purpose: `ostra-code` keeps one index per project: each file's mentioned names, definitions, resolved imports, and supertypes. It builds a dependency graph from them. The Files view in the console reads the index through a chain of providers. Agents read it through the eight code tools. It uses a table-driven tokenizer and per-family rules instead of a compiler, so it answers while a project fails to build.

assumptions: The index never keeps file text. A usages query re-reads only files whose name set contains the name.
Files over MAX_FILE_BYTES (1 MiB) are skipped. Indexing stops at MAX_INDEX_BYTES (256 MiB) per project, and answers say so.
A usages query reads at most MAX_SCAN_FILES (4000) files, and a transitive walk visits at most MAX_REACH (5000).
A name defined in more than MAX_DEF_FILES (3) files links none of them unless the mentioning file imports the definer.
The code tools always read the built-in index, even when a language server is configured.

sections.purpose: A workspace is a folder with .ostra/workspace.toml, a row in the machine registry, and registry records that hold its control settings. `ostra-workspace` owns WorkspaceRt, the runtime of one open workspace. It also owns the trust rules that keep control settings and unapproved commands out of folder files, workspace creation and deletion, and project import.

sections.title: Storage
sections.purpose: `ostra-store` opens every SQLite database through rusqlite with SQLite compiled in. There are three kinds. The first is the workspace database (<workspace>/.ostra/workspace.db), which holds the event log and the tables built from it. The second is the machine registry (registry.db in the data dir), which holds workspaces, push subscriptions, sign-ins, and sealed credentials. The third is each project's lesson store (<project>/.ostra/memory/knowledge.sqlite3).

owns: WorkspaceDb, its migrations, and every query on workspace.db

assumptions: Each migration runs in its own transaction and bumps user_version in that same transaction. Migrations are only appended.
Databases run in WAL mode with a 5-second busy timeout, so reads never block the engine's writes.
Tool call output is cut to TOOL_OUTPUT_LIMIT (8 KiB) before it is stored.
MemoryStore opens a fresh connection per call, so parallel executions wait on SQLite's file lock.
A sealed value starts with enc:v1:, and the row key is the associated data, so a value copied into another row fails to decrypt.

sections.title: Web Push notifications
sections.purpose: `ostra-notify` sends Web Push to the user's browsers and phones. It sends a notice when a gate opens that YOLO will not answer, when a phase is blocked, and when a session completes or fails. It implements RFC 8291 encryption, RFC 8188 aes128gcm coding, and RFC 8292 VAPID with pure-Rust crates, so the binary needs no OpenSSL.

The count of consecutive failing build or test commands in one execution; at 5 build commands are refused.
A tool call in Claude Code's tool names and input shapes, with absolute paths, which is the only form the policy judges.
A tool family an agent's agent.toml grants, which each executor maps to its own tool name.
The per-project index of definitions, mentions, imports, and supertypes that the Files view and the code tools read.
One source of Files view answers in the chain: a project program, a language server, or the built-in index.
A secret-read, self-protection, or git-metadata denial, a private egress refusal, or a decoy open; three in one execution pause the session (Rule P3).
A fake credential file planted in a hidden path whose opening raises a containment signal.
The per-execution proxy that is a sandboxed process's only route to the network and allows or refuses each host.
A message an engine broadcasts: Event, Delta, ExecutionStatus, SessionUpdated, or ProjectsChanged.
One agent run from its first message to its result, on the native or a harness executor.
A unit of the per-workspace concurrency limit limits.max_parallel_executions, taken by acquire_slot before a spawn runs.
The trait with one run method that runs one agent; implemented by NativeExecutor and HarnessExecutor.
SessionState::fold, which replays a session's events into its current state with no outside input.
A question the session waits on, typed as a GatePayload, answered by the user, YOLO, or the engine.
A layer 1 policy rule that no permission, answer, mode, or YOLO can override.
An installed coding CLI (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build, or Antigravity) that Ostra runs in a PTY as an executor.
The path from a harness hook through ostra hook and /internal/policy to the policy and back.
One structured model call with a forced decide tool that answers a named question such as Classify or Rescue.
A guard that refuses an ok submit after a recovery from 3 or more failures until a lesson is recorded.
The server component that holds one connection per workspace MCP server and hands tools to executions.
Ostra's own agent loop over a provider API, its own tools, and the policy.
The layer 2 setting default, acceptEdits, plan, or bypass that decides what asks.
One step of an approved plan, or one inline change, built in one project by one work loop.
The only facts from outside the event log the planner may read: each project's format command and the session budget.

The implement and review loop of one phase, WorkLoop in state.rs.
